payload.text:
The ford comes up amber and loud, river swollen past its stones, and the birds that should be scolding you from the willows have simply stopped. The ferry sits chained to its post. The ferry-house door hangs open on one hinge, and inside, rope lies cut in a clean curl, the strongbox pried and gaping. No one calls down to haggle over fare. Low along the threshold, pressed into mud gone soft with river-damp, small clawed tracks lead away from the box and out toward the causeway, then stop at the planks as if whatever made them simply stepped up onto stone and vanished.

Above, in the dark of the loft, a floorboard creaks.

payload.body: The ford runs high and loud, swollen past its stones. The ferry sits chained to its post, silent—no bell-ringer calls down. Inside the ferry-house, ropes lie cut clean, the strongbox pried open and emptied. Small clawed tracks press into the mud outside, leading from the box toward the causeway planks, then vanish. A floorboard creaks in the dark loft above.

payload.text:
The loft goes still, then a ladder's rungs take weight, slow, testing. Wenna climbs down backward, skirts hiked with one hand, smelling of pitch and river-fear, counting the rungs under her breath — one, two, three. She stops close, eyes hard on Tamsin's face like she's weighing a coin for the clip.

"Pell first," she says, voice clipped to the bone. "You bring my boy home, then we talk ferry." She jerks her chin toward the causeway. "Timbers are sunk — they'll sing your steps to anything listening. Reed channel left of the third post runs quiet. Goes to the island."

She says no more, and will not be asked twice.

Reed channel it is — I'd rather get wet quiet than loud.

She demanded Pell's return before she would help with the ferry crossing again.

The reeds break apart in a scramble of small bodies — goblins boiling up from a dugout camp half-sunk in the mud, more startled than fierce. One wiry shape shoves a boy behind a leaning post, keeping its own bulk between him and the water. "Big-feet! Big-feet come stomping!" shrieks a goblin wearing a leather strap like a belt, the ferry's clapper swinging loose at his hip. Above, in the reed-dark, a lookout's shape shifts — and a thrown dagger whips down past Tamsin's shoulder, burying itself in mud instead of flesh.

The goblins at the post go rigid, waiting to see what the near-miss buys them.

Odo spreads his hands wide, palms up, and lets Wenna's name carry over the mud and reeds like a thrown rope. The shrieking falters. Snag's ears twitch at the name; he barks something low, and the wiry shapes around the post go still, blades lowering a notch at a time. The goblin with the clapper-strap plants himself between the party and the boy, chin jutting, sing-song bravado gone thin and brittle.

"Big-feet say Wenna-name," Snag mutters, mostly to himself, mostly to be brave. "Snag listen. Big-feet walk slow. Clapper stays." Behind him, Pell strains against his binding rope, trying to look older than his years, trying not to need saving.

payload.text: I press on toward the ferry before dark.

The sunk-timber causeway stretches out under the last red light, planks black with water, the bell tower a dead shape behind you. Your feet find the first timber and stop there — the world will not carry you past this threshold unasked. From the reeds a sing-song voice curls out, naming you big-feet, savoring the word like a game already won. Closer, half-swallowed by rushes, a boy's voice cracks too loud, fighting to sound older than it is, a red-ragged spear catching the dying light. Snag doesn't budge, pole planted between Tamsin and the cold chain, the clapper-strap creaking at his belt. Behind him the light goes the color of old rust, the reeds already losing their shapes to shadow. Wenna's counting falters under her breath, losing the thread of threes. Snag's sing-song thins to almost nothing, his eyes flicking toward the dark tree-line where no bell rings. The ferry waits, patient and useless, while the name Pell sits unanswered between them all, and the last of the dusk is going fast.

Tamsin — what do you actually do, facing Snag, with the light nearly gone?
